title: goal — why we are asking, and what we want to know (4.5.1, 5.1)

purpose.description: Cannot be inferred; a missing purpose is a question for the human (4.5.1)

intent.description: Defaults from purpose. Differing from the default requires intent_rationale (check 32).

definition.description: Kept for now and no longer required: the definition lives in contracts/observables.json, and a card that restates it holds a second copy that drifts -- eight cards had already drifted from the vocabulary by 2026-09-18. Name the observable and the definition, the estimator and the window come with it by reference. This property is due to be removed once every card has dropped it; 5.4 still asks for the definition and that sentence is the architecture seat's to settle before then.

targets.description: What accuracy is wanted. In explore mode, stated in decades. A target is a DECISION and not a claim about the world, so it carries no source and no grade -- the same reason a ceiling in envelope/safety.json carries none. A grade measures how far a claim can be trusted; a decision is correct by being made, and grading a person's own goal E5 would say they might be misremembering what they want. Inline rather than by reference so that a grade is not merely absent but inexpressible: an opt-in guard is not a chokepoint (2.1 rule 9).

oneOf.$comment: SUPERSEDED, and to be deleted. This form names an entry in numbers[], which P2 makes four-part -- so it forces a source and a grade onto a decision, which is what the inline form exists to stop. REMOVE THIS BRANCH once microscope_agent/questions/mic-20260918-001/goal.json and simulation_agent/questions/sim-20260917-001/goal.json carry the inline form; they are the only two cards using it. Kept meanwhile because the schema is contracts/ and those cards are two other seats' trees, so check 35 makes this at least three commits, and the gate runs the whole validator -- a schema that rejects a live card blocks every session from committing for the length of the migration. Two shapes at once is what 11-11 counts, and here the alternative is a full stop. Written open-ended, 'meanwhile' becomes permanent. manager-bridge, 2026-09-19, ruled by architecture.

priority.description: Ordered. Safety is deliberately absent: it is a constraint, not a tradeable item (2.1).

compare_variable.description: required when purpose is compare: the one parameter allowed to differ between arms (check 34)

constraint_notes.description: Free-text limits from the human. Named apart from the interval lists elsewhere: same word, different kind of thing.

configuration_preference.description: An ordered tie-break from the person, read by S3.0 ONLY when the cap is unresolved (4.5.1 branch c). It settles which of several capable configurations to spend the fan-out on. It never overrides a capability refusal: a preference naming a configuration the screen rejected, or one absent from the table, is recorded and refused rather than honoured, and screening stops at that entry instead of sliding to the next -- a card asking for a configuration the instrument cannot use is a card to fix, and quietly granting its second choice hides that. It is not evidence: it raises no grade, supports no number, is not an assumption with a falsifier, and S4 may not cite it.

sample_contrast_provenance.description: Where sample_contrast came from. It is a claim about the world -- these beads carry a fluorophore -- so it is graded like any other claim (P2). An operator reading an instrument and an operator recalling a preparation are not the same source and do not get the same grade: a statement from memory is E5. Required in practice whenever sample_contrast is present; left optional for one step only, because making it required today would fail a goal card already committed in another seat's path. Tighten once that card carries it.

configuration_preference_by.description: Who chose the tie-break, and when. Deliberately NOT a source and a grade: a preference is not a claim about the world, so there is nothing to grade and nothing to falsify (4.5.1 c). What it needs is attribution, so that a later reader can ask the person rather than mistake the choice for a finding. `reason` is optional and stays empty when none was given -- an invented reason would be worse than the silence.

sample_contrast.description: What this sample offers, as a set. A configuration survives the contrast screen when its requires_contrast is one of these -- membership, not equality. A set because a fluorescent tracer still has refractive-index contrast and so provides both, which is why equality would drop brightfield from a fluorescent question. S3.0 can evaluate this before S3 runs, which none of the priority terms can (4.5.3).

from_round.description: Present when this goal was written from a delivered round (5.1): the thread and round it came from. It is how the bridge learns the round was taken. The bridge already reads the executing agents' questions/ (6.2-3), so this closes the loop with no write across a boundary and no second copy of whose turn it is -- the thread ledger stays the only place that says that.
